name: Lipoabdominoplasty

card.summary: A tummy tuck combined with liposuction to remove loose skin and fat and sharpen the waist and midsection contour.
card.note: Major surgery; seroma and wound problems are among documented complications.

quick.overview:
Lipoabdominoplasty combines abdominoplasty (tummy tuck) with liposuction. Excess lower abdominal skin is removed and the abdominal wall tightened, while liposuction thins fat and refines the contour of the abdomen, flanks and waist.

The appearance payoff is a flatter, more defined midsection and slimmer waist, particularly after pregnancy or weight loss.
quick.how: A surgeon uses a hip-to-hip incision, repositions the navel and tightens the abdominal wall, with liposuction used to sculpt the trunk. Variants limit undermining or add anatomical definition. Surgeons describe recovery with a dressing, drainage and sometimes a compression garment.
quick.risks: Complication rates for abdominoplasty are described as higher than many cosmetic procedures. Seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed healing, necrosis, scarring, sensory change, blood clots and anaesthesia risks are listed. Smoking, obesity and diabetes raise risk.

lead: Lipoabdominoplasty is a body-contouring operation that combines abdominoplasty (a tummy tuck) with liposuction in a single session to flatten and define the abdomen, flanks and waist [1][2]. Abdominoplasty removes excess skin and fat from the middle and lower abdomen and usually tightens the weakened abdominal muscle and fascia, while liposuction thins the fat layer and shapes the surrounding trunk [2][3].

People seek it for a flatter stomach and a more defined waist when diet and training do not change loose skin or a stretched abdominal wall, commonly after pregnancy or major weight loss [3][3]. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons describes a tummy tuck as a way to remove excess fat and skin and restore weakened muscles, and states that it is not a substitute for weight loss or exercise [4]. Combining it with liposuction has become common: a 2020 review notes abdominoplasty is among the most frequently performed cosmetic operations in the United States and that liposuction is its most common adjunct [5].

A 2020 historical review credits Pitanguy with popularising abdominoplasty in 1967, Illouz's 1983 suction-assisted lipectomy with opening the way to combined procedures, and Matarasso with advancing the safe pairing of liposuction with full abdominoplasty [1]. Later surgeons developed selective undermining and preservation of blood vessels to reduce complications [1][6]. Published studies have compared limited-undermining lipoabdominoplasty with traditional abdominoplasty for skin-flap blood flow and seroma [7][8].

chain: Loose skin and fat removed, abdominal wall tightened
angle.text: It targets the abdomen and waist by removing skin and fat in one operation, producing a flatter, more contoured trunk.

infobox: Typically general anaesthesia in a surgical facility [3]
Commonly hip to hip above the pubic area for full abdominoplasty [2]
Loose abdominal skin, fat and muscle laxity after pregnancy or weight loss [3]

paras: A complete abdominoplasty uses a hip-to-hip incision above the pubic area. The surgeon lifts the skin and fat layer, repositions the navel, tightens the abdominal muscle and fascia with sutures, removes the excess lower abdominal skin and closes the wound, often with drains and a dressing or compression garment [2]. In lipoabdominoplasty, liposuction is added to refine the abdomen, flanks and waist, and in some techniques liposuction of the flap replaces part of the traditional undermining [1][6].

Surgeons use classification systems to decide which tissue layers to treat. One described system categorises candidates by whether skin, fat or muscle is the treatable problem and matches them to the appropriate level of operation; postpartum abdominal wall changes are described as best addressed by abdominoplasty [3].

Recognised abdominoplasty variants include the mini (partial) procedure with a shorter incision, the extended version that addresses the flanks, high lateral tension abdominoplasty described by Lockwood in 1995 to improve hip and flank contour, the floating-navel approach, and circumferential or belt lipectomy used after massive weight loss [2].

Lipoabdominoplasty with anatomical definition (LADE) is a technique described by its proponents as highlighting the abdominal musculature for a more natural result while preserving perforating blood vessels and suspending Scarpa's fascia to reduce morbidity [6]. Another approach from the Institut Vila-Rovira combines extensive liposuction with minimal abdominoplasty and is described for patients with a body mass index of 30 to 35 [9]. Reports have also described endoscopic and radiofrequency-assisted versions [10][11].

Pitanguy popularised abdominoplasty in 1967, first as an adjunct to ventral hernia repair and then for aesthetic improvement of the abdomen [1]. Illouz introduced suction-assisted lipectomy in 1983, after which liposuction was used with mini-abdominoplasty and later with full abdominoplasty [1]. Liposuction itself grew from work in Rome in the 1970s by Arpad and Giorgio Fischer and from Illouz's wet technique; tumescent local anaesthesia was developed by American dermatologists in the 1980s [12].

Matarasso systematised combinations of undermining, excision and liposuction according to the degree of skin laxity and muscle separation. Lockwood advocated high lateral tension closure of the superficial fascial system, and Saldanha advanced selective undermining and perforator preservation [1].

A review of combined surgery reports that liposuction is the most common adjunct to abdominoplasty, followed by breast surgery, lower back lift and thigh lift, with hernia repair and gynecologic procedures also paired with it [5]. Combined sessions that treat the abdomen and breasts are often marketed as a mommy makeover [2]. The review frames the goal as broader aesthetic improvement while weighing the added risk of longer surgery [5]. Secondary or revision body contouring has its own literature on managing shortcomings and patient expectations [13].

Dressings, drains and compression garments are described as part of the post-operative course [2]. Pain control is a focus of research: a randomised trial examined ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane nerve blocks in lipoabdominoplasty [14]. Trials have also tested fibrin glue in circular abdominoplasty after massive weight loss for seroma reduction [15].

Listed complications of abdominoplasty include seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed wound healing, skin or fat necrosis, scarring, changes in sensation, asymmetry, blood clots including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and anaesthesia-related problems [2]. Smoking, obesity, diabetes, prior abdominal surgery and combining procedures are described as raising risk [2].

Liposuction carries its own reported risks, including fat embolism, bleeding, infection and, in large-volume cases, higher complication rates [12]. The CDC has reported deaths of US citizens after cosmetic surgery in the Dominican Republic, most of those confirmed at autopsy being from embolism, a point relevant to patients who travel abroad for body contouring [12]. The American Society of Plastic Surgeons states that significant weight change or future pregnancy can reduce the lasting result and advises people planning either to consider postponing surgery [4].

A prospective controlled study of 18 non-smoking patients compared abdominal flap perfusion and overall complications between limited-undermining lipoabdominoplasty and traditional abdominoplasty using laser fluorescence imaging, to address safety concerns about the single-stage combination [7]. A comparative study used ultrasound to assess seroma formation in lipoabdominoplasty versus abdominoplasty [8]. A 2019 clinical trial examined diaphragm mobility and lung function in healthy women after lipoabdominoplasty [16]. A randomised trial evaluated TAP block analgesia in the operation [14], and a 2026 randomised trial looked at nanofat for wound healing [17]. A review of the Vila-Rovira technique and a 2024 update on anatomical definition describe surgeon-reported technique and results [6][9].

Lipoabdominoplasty appears occasionally in looksmax.org discussion as a body procedure rather than a facial one. In one thread a user weighed paying for his wife's liposuction and tummy tuck abroad alongside his own planned facial surgeries, comparing costs and travel [18]. T Nation forum members have discussed tummy tucks and liposuction in the context of cosmetic surgery generally and of loose skin after large fat loss [19][20].

timeline.event: Pitanguy popularises abdominoplasty, first as an aid to ventral hernia repair and then for aesthetics [1].
Arpad and Giorgio Fischer develop blunt-cannula suction lipectomy in Rome [12].
Illouz introduces suction-assisted lipectomy; combined procedures follow [1].
Tumescent local anaesthesia is developed by American dermatologists [12].
Lockwood describes high lateral tension abdominoplasty [2].
Vila-Rovira technique of extensive liposuction with minimal abdominoplasty described in Clinics in Plastic Surgery [9].
Laser fluorescence study compares limited-undermining lipoabdominoplasty with traditional abdominoplasty [7].
Review of standards and trends in lipoabdominoplasty published [1].
Update on lipoabdominoplasty with anatomical definition published [6].

lore.intro: Lipoabdominoplasty is discussed in looksmaxxing and fitness forums mainly as a route to remove loose skin and sharpen the waist, often alongside cost and travel considerations [18][20].

claims.claim: Skin and fat left after major weight loss cannot be fixed by training and surgery is the route.
claims.believers: Forum members describe a stubborn fold of loose tissue around the waist after large weight loss that limits leanness in the abdomen [20].
claims.experts: The ASPS says a tummy tuck removes excess skin and fat and restores weakened muscle, and that it is not a substitute for weight loss or exercise [4].

claims.claim: Doing liposuction and a tummy tuck together gives a better contour in one operation.
claims.believers: Surgeons and patients describe combining the two to sculpt abdomen, flanks and waist in a single session [1][5].
claims.experts: Reviews describe liposuction as the most common adjunct to abdominoplasty and note extra risk from longer surgery; studies have compared flap blood flow and seroma between the combined and traditional approaches [5][7][8].

claims.claim: Surgery abroad is a way to afford body contouring.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster planned procedures in the Dominican Republic and elsewhere to cut costs [18].
claims.experts: The CDC reported 93 US citizen deaths after cosmetic surgery in the Dominican Republic from 2009 to 2022, most autopsy-confirmed ones from embolism [12].

claims.claim: Preserving blood vessels makes the combined operation safer.
claims.believers: Proponents of anatomical-definition techniques say preserving perforators and suspending Scarpa's fascia lowers morbidity [6].
claims.experts: A prospective study compared flap perfusion between limited-undermining lipoabdominoplasty and traditional abdominoplasty [7].
